solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Disclose bonus after sacking some internally (7)

indicatorNotes.sacking: to sack a place is to wreck it, so the letters of 'bonus' are thrown about
indicatorNotes.internally: only the inside of 'some' is used

blocks.note: the five letters of BONUS rearranged
anagram indicator
the middle two letters of sOMe
tells you to take the inside of 'some'

annotation.surface: A company lays people off and keeps quiet about a bonus paid out after the redundancies.
annotation.walkthrough: 'After' is the tricky word: in the surface it means following the layoffs, but here it only places the OM behind the rearranged BONUS. To unbosom yourself is an old phrase for pouring out your secrets.
annotation.definitionFit: To unbosom is to disclose what you had kept in your breast, your secrets or feelings.

entries.clue: Depose international body established to protect America (6)

indicatorNotes.to protect: SET guards A by wrapping round it

blocks.note: the United Nations
set = established, as in a set routine; it wraps round A
A is a standard abbreviation for America
container indicator: SET goes round A

annotation.surface: A plan to topple a leader, with the UN set up to shield the United States.
annotation.walkthrough: The UN in the surface sounds like the actor; it only supplies the first two letters, and the container sits after it.
annotation.definitionFit: To unseat a ruler or official is to depose them, knock them out of their seat of power.

entries.clue: Dumb ox came racing around one taking shots (3,6)

indicatorNotes.around: the answer is lying around inside the words, there among them

blocks.note: dumB OX CAME RAcing: the answer runs across the four words
hidden-word indicator

annotation.surface: A mute ox stampedes about, like a cartoon beast charging round a field.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Around' looks like it describes where the ox is racing, and invites an anagram; it really says the answer is lying about in the words. 'Taking shots' sounds like a gunman, but a camera takes photographs.
annotation.definitionFit: A box camera is a simple early camera, one that takes shots, that is photographs.

entries.clue: Was proud and snobbish (5-2)

blocks.note: proud in the builder's sense: a nail is proud when it sticks out of the wood
haughty, looking down on others

annotation.surface: A description of someone vain and superior.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Proud' is used in the builder's sense, sticking out beyond a surface, not in the sense of vain; that is what makes it a different meaning from 'snobbish'.
annotation.definitionFit: Something proud sticks out, so 'was proud' is 'stuck up'; and a stuck-up person is snobbish.

entries.clue: Don’s partner on university study is sluggish? (9)

blocks.note: a moll is a gangster's girlfriend; a Don is a Mafia boss
U = university
to scan = to study closely

annotation.surface: An Oxford or Cambridge don's partner, doing university work, is accused of being lazy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like a university lecturer, which the word 'university' encourages; it is a Mafia Don, whose partner is his moll. 'Sluggish?' means like a slug, and the question mark flags the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: Slugs are molluscs, so something slug-like is molluscan; the question mark admits the stretch.

entries.clue: Eat something from this meal (4,3)

blocks.note: EAT is what you get from the answer when you read it as an instruction: a word, then an anagram indicator meaning drunk
the definition: a British meal

annotation.surface: An invitation to help yourself to something on the table at a meal.
annotation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer is the wordplay and the clue is its result. Read HIGH TEA as an instruction, 'high' meaning drunk and so muddled, applied to TEA, and you get EAT.
annotation.definitionFit: High tea is an early-evening British meal of a cooked dish with bread, cakes and tea.

entries.clue: Without being out of pocket, get around obstacle (5)

annotation.definition: Without being out of pocket, get around

blocks.clueFragment: Without being out of pocket, get around
blocks.note: travel for free by thumbing lifts from passing drivers
a snag, something that holds a plan up

annotation.surface: Advice on how to get past a barrier without spending any money.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Get around obstacle' reads as one phrase, a way past a barrier; the split falls between 'around' and 'obstacle', and the first half describes hitchhiking.
annotation.definitionFit: Hitching a ride costs nothing, so you travel without being out of pocket; and a hitch is an obstacle.

entries.clue: State embracing Republican — evil, thuggish individual (7)

indicatorNotes.embracing: GOA holds R and ILL in its arms

blocks.note: Goa is a state of India; it wraps round the rest
R = Republican
ill = evil, as in ill deeds
container indicator

annotation.surface: Talk of an American state with a Republican in charge and a nasty brute at large.
annotation.walkthrough: With 'Republican' beside it, 'State' looks American; it is Goa, the small state on India's west coast.
annotation.definitionFit: A gorilla is slang for a big, brutish heavy, a thug.

entries.clue: Attempt to persuade did work for those attending (5)

indicatorNotes.for those attending: to attend is to listen, so this is how it sounds to a listener

blocks.note: temped = did temporary office work
homophone indicator

annotation.surface: Someone did a job for those who turned up, as a way of winning them over.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Attending' seems to mean those present at an event; here it means those listening. To temp is to work as a temporary office worker.
annotation.definitionFit: To tempt someone is to try to persuade them, usually with something attractive.

entries.clue: Transforming complex integral repositioned triangle (8)

indicatorNotes.complex: complex = intricate, tangled, so the letters are jumbled
indicatorNotes.repositioned: the letters of 'triangle' are moved into new places

blocks.note: the eight letters of INTEGRAL rearranged
anagram indicator
a second anagram: TRIANGLE has the same eight letters as INTEGRAL, and 'repositioned' shuffles them

annotation.surface: A maths lesson on transforming a complex integral and moving a triangle about.
annotation.walkthrough: INTEGRAL, TRIANGLE and ALTERING use the same eight letters, so the setter gives two anagrams side by side; either one alone gets you there.
annotation.definitionFit: Altering and transforming both mean changing something.

entries.clue: One of several young relations returned deposit with rent (9)

indicatorNotes.returned: PUT is turned back to TUP

blocks.note: relations = sexual relations
deposit = PUT (put down), turned back
to let = to rent out

annotation.surface: Young relatives get their deposit back on a rented flat.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'young relations' as one phrase, family members; the definition stops at 'young', meaning offspring, and 'relations' starts the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A sextuplet is one of six babies born at one birth, one of several young.

entries.clue: Recorder of minutes perhaps lying about terms of reference (5)

indicatorNotes.lying about: about = turned round, so TIMER lies the other way

blocks.note: a timer records minutes; 'perhaps' because it could record seconds or hours
reversal indicator

annotation.surface: A minute-taker at a meeting is caught misrepresenting the committee's terms of reference.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Recorder of minutes' paints a committee secretary taking notes; it is a kitchen timer. A remit is the scope of a job or inquiry.
annotation.definitionFit: A remit is the set task or area of authority given to someone, their terms of reference.

entries.clue: NZ union man missing every line once behind (5)

indicatorNotes.missing every line: 'missing' means without, and 'every' insists that all the Ls go, since L is the abbreviation for line

blocks.note: an All Black is a player in New Zealand's rugby union team
L = line; all three Ls come out of ALLBLACK, leaving five letters

annotation.surface: A New Zealand rugby player misses every line-out, having once been a back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks the definition as old usage: aback used to mean backwards or behind, before it survived mainly in 'taken aback'.
annotation.definitionFit: Aback is an archaic word for backwards or behind, hence 'once'.

entries.clue: Cover overcoat when carrying overhead projector around (9)

indicatorNotes.carrying: ULSTER carries the projector inside it
indicatorNotes.around: OHP is turned round to PHO

blocks.note: an ulster is a long, loose overcoat; it goes round the rest
OHP (overhead projector) turned round
container indicator

annotation.surface: Someone wraps an overhead projector in a coat to carry it.
annotation.walkthrough: OHP is the usual abbreviation for an overhead projector, the classroom machine that throws transparencies onto a screen.
annotation.definitionFit: To upholster a chair is to cover it with padding and fabric.

entries.clue: Look forward to lecture material delivered by Hawking (13)

blocks.note: to expect = to look forward to
an oration = a formal speech or lecture

annotation.surface: Anticipating a lecture given by Stephen Hawking, the physicist.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital H makes 'Hawking' look like the physicist, fitting 'lecture'; hawking is clearing your throat and coughing up phlegm, and the material brought up is expectoration.
annotation.definitionFit: Expectoration is phlegm coughed up, the stuff produced by hawking.

entries.clue: Mediator reconciled son with bad mum (9)

indicatorNotes.reconciled: the letters are brought together into a new arrangement

blocks.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A mediator patches things up between a son and his bad mother.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is exactly what an ombudsman does, settling a dispute, so the definition hides in plain sight.
annotation.definitionFit: An ombudsman investigates complaints and mediates between the public and an organisation.

entries.clue: Popular writer’s hosting channel using conclusive methods (9)

indicatorNotes.hosting: IN and I'VE together play host to DUCT, holding it between them

blocks.note: in = fashionable, popular
the writer has = I'VE; with IN it goes round DUCT
a duct = a channel or pipe; it sits between IN and I'VE
container indicator

annotation.surface: A bestselling author is hosting a TV channel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Writer's' stands for 'writer has', the writer being the setter, I; so I'VE, not a possessive. 'Channel' looks like television.
annotation.definitionFit: Inductive reasoning draws general conclusions from particular cases, so it uses methods that reach conclusions.

entries.clue: This admirer makes marriage vow subsequently (8)

blocks.note: 'I do', said at a wedding
later = subsequently

annotation.surface: An admirer makes a wedding vow and only later thinks about it.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface hints at a proposal from a devoted admirer; the vow and 'subsequently' just sit one after the other.
annotation.definitionFit: An idolater worships idols, an extreme admirer.

entries.clue: Part of kitchen cabinet reducing liquidity of executives? (8,5)

blocks.note: the ridged surface beside a sink where washed dishes drain
a board of executives that drains the company's cash, read literally

annotation.surface: A 'kitchen cabinet', a leader's informal group of advisers, draining the executives' cash.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Kitchen cabinet' reads as one phrase, but the split falls between the two words. The second half is whimsical: a board of directors that drains away money, hence the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: A draining board is the sloped area next to a kitchen sink where dishes drip dry.

entries.clue: Source of power is vague after leader steps down (7)

indicatorNotes.after leader steps down: the first letter moves down one place

blocks.note: unclear = vague
the first letter, U, drops one place in this down entry and trades places with N

annotation.surface: A report on an energy source is vague once the leader has resigned.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Steps down' looks like resigning, and deleting the first letter; here the leader only moves one step down the entry, swapping places with N.
annotation.definitionFit: Nuclear power is a source of energy, so 'nuclear' works as shorthand for it.

entries.clue: Use of line going off at a tangent (7)

blocks.note: fishing with a rod and line
heading off sideways, slanting away from the straight path

annotation.surface: A geometry lesson on a line that leaves a curve at a tangent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Line' and 'tangent' both belong to geometry, but the first definition is a fishing line.
annotation.definitionFit: Angling is fishing with a line; and something angling off is veering away at an angle.

entries.clue: Give up on first of those left behind (6)

indicatorNotes.first of: take only the first letter of 'those'

blocks.note: to forgo = to give up, do without
the first letter of Those

annotation.surface: Someone gives up on the first of those who were abandoned.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On' only places T after FORGO. To forget something is to leave it behind, as with an umbrella on a train.
annotation.definitionFit: Forgot means left behind by mistake: I forgot my keys at home.

entries.clue: Accommodation on boat where one throws up? (6,3)

blocks.note: a launch is a motorboat
pad = slang for a flat or home
PAD goes after LAUNCH

annotation.surface: A seasick passenger's cabin on a boat, where they are sick.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Throws up' pairs with 'boat' to suggest seasickness; a launch pad is where rockets are sent up.
annotation.definitionFit: A launch pad is the platform from which rockets are launched, thrown up into the sky.

entries.clue: Surprising result increases trade deficit in the end (5)

indicatorNotes.in the end: take the end of each of the two words

blocks.note: ups = increases, as in ups the price
the last letters of tradE and deficiT

annotation.surface: An unexpected outcome widens the trade deficit in the long run.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In the end' reads as 'eventually'; here it takes the last letter of each of 'trade' and 'deficit'. An upset in sport is a win for the underdog.
annotation.definitionFit: An upset is an unexpected result, such as a favourite losing.

entries.clue: Shaved heads of punks appeared revolutionary (5)

indicatorNotes.heads of: take the heads, the first letters, of the next two words

blocks.note: the first letters of Punks and Appeared
a red = a revolutionary communist

annotation.surface: Punks with shaved heads looked like revolutionaries.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shaved heads' looks like a single phrase, but 'Shaved' is the definition and 'heads' starts the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Pared means trimmed or shaved thinly, as with pared cheese or a pared-down budget.

entries.clue: Cold-blooded individual in City bank ultimately consumed by success (5)

indicatorNotes.consumed by: something consumed is swallowed, so EC and K end up inside GO

blocks.note: go = success, as in make a go of it; it wraps round the rest
EC is the postcode of the City of London
the last letter of banK
container indicator

annotation.surface: A heartless banker in the City who lives only for success, like Gordon Gekko in 'Wall Street'.
annotation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, and its postcodes begin EC. 'Cold-blooded' paints a ruthless banker; a gecko is a lizard, a cold-blooded reptile.
annotation.definitionFit: A gecko is a lizard, and reptiles are cold-blooded creatures.

entries.clue: Have a little bit of judgment (5)

blocks.note: try a small amount of food
discernment, good judgment in matters of style

annotation.surface: A plea for just a little bit of good sense.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'a little bit of judgment' as one phrase; 'of' is only the join between the two meanings.
annotation.definitionFit: To taste is to have a small bite; and taste is aesthetic judgment.

entries.clue: Outstanding anti-Brexit government originally getting elected (9)

indicatorNotes.getting: to get is to receive, so REMAIN and G take IN in between them

blocks.note: Remain was the side opposing Brexit in the 2016 UK referendum on leaving the EU
in = elected, voted into office; it goes between REMAIN and G
the first letter of Government
container indicator

annotation.surface: An excellent pro-European government wins the election.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' reads as excellent, praising the government; it means still to be done, as in outstanding bills.
annotation.definitionFit: Outstanding means still left over, as remaining debts or tasks are.

entries.clue: Soldiers ready to drop out of service? (7)

blocks.note: RE = Royal Engineers, a British army corps
ready to drop = exhausted, tired

annotation.surface: Worn-out soldiers about to leave the armed services.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is almost literal, which is the trick: 'service' is the military one, and the retired are no longer in it.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone retired has left work, out of service; the question mark allows for the loose phrasing.

entries.clue: Ignore article made into chapter in elegant novel (7)

indicatorNotes.made into: to make one thing into another is to convert it, so the article A is converted into C
indicatorNotes.novel: novel = new, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: the word to work on
the article A becomes C (chapter), giving ELEGCNT
anagram indicator: the seven letters of ELEGCNT are rearranged

annotation.surface: An author ignores the advice to turn an article into a chapter of an elegant novel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book, especially after 'chapter'; it means new, and tells you to rearrange. C is the standard abbreviation for chapter.
annotation.definitionFit: To neglect something is to ignore it or fail to attend to it.
